Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft 1.14.3.
2. Launch any world.
3. Place an item on an anvil.
4. Rename the item with any 18 character string.
5. Attempt to delete all text using Shift + Command + Delete.
6. Observe that the game crashes, displaying "saving world".
Observed Behavior: When attempting to delete an 18-character string in an anvil using the Shift Command Delete function, the game crashes with a "saving world" message. This issue can be reproduced by launching Minecraft version 1.14.3, entering any world in any game mode, placing an item on the anvil, renaming it with an 18-character string, and then using the Shift Command Delete to remove all text. The crash report indicates a java.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, specifically noting that the string index is out of range, which occurs during the rendering process. The stack trace reveals that the error originates from the String.substring method, as well as various rendering methods that follow. The crash affects all players in the session, and the game operates within the Minecraft: overworld dimension, with the specific world being a multiplayer server. The issue appears to be consistent across different player locations within the world, and the game mode is set to survival without any cheats enabled. This bug highlights a critical flaw in the text handling system within the anvil interface, necessitating further investigation by the development team to prevent future occurrences.
Expected Behavior: When the player renames an item on an anvil by entering an 18-character string and uses the Shift + Delete command to remove all text, the game should successfully delete the text without crashing. The anvil interface should remain responsive, allowing the player to continue editing or renaming items without any interruptions or errors. This behavior should be consistent in Minecraft version 1.14.3.
